title: The stack diagonal preserves closed points
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $\mathcal X$ be a finite-type algebraic stack over $k$ [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Suppose its diagonal $\Delta_{\mathcal X/k}:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\times_k\mathcal X$ is quasi-finite and separated: after scheme charts it is finite type with finite geometric fibres and has closed relative diagonal. Then $|\Delta_{\mathcal X/k}|$ sends closed points of $|\mathcal X|$ to closed points of $|\mathcal X\times_k\mathcal X|$. The point space consists of field-valued objects up to isomorphism after common field extension, with topology detected by a smooth scheme atlas; closed means that the singleton is closed. The product is the 2-fibre product over $\operatorname{Spec}k$. No adequate moduli space is assumed to exist.

source.place: Theorem 8.3.2, proof of (3) implies (1), sentence immediately before the product adequate-moduli diagram, printed pp.39--40. This is the topological diagonal assertion, independently of the existence of an adequate moduli space. Primary PDF read online at https://arxiv.org/pdf/1005.2398v3; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Fix a closed point $x\in|\mathcal X|$. By [lem-sfb-smooth-presentation-closed-subsets] the closed singleton $\{x\}$ has a reduced closed substack $i:\mathcal Z\hookrightarrow\mathcal X$ with $|\mathcal Z|$ a singleton. By [lem-sfb-stack-closed-immersion-calculus], $\mathcal Z$ is locally of finite type over $k$, since $\mathcal X$ is finite type. Apply [lem-sfb-singleton-stack-finite-field-homeomorphism] to obtain a finite extension $K/k$ and a universally homeomorphic $k$-morphism $\pi:\mathcal Z\to\operatorname{Spec}K$.

source.place: Tag 0509 (lemma-reduced-closed-substack); stacks-morphisms.tex Tags 06QK and 06R9, via the two cited supporting lemmas.

proof.text: Form $\mathcal Z\times_k\mathcal Z$ and $\mathcal X\times_k\mathcal X$, which are algebraic stacks by [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-fibre-products] (schemes, in particular $\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $\operatorname{Spec}K$, are viewed as discrete algebraic stacks in the definition [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]). The map $j=i\times_k i$ factors as $\mathcal Z\times_k\mathcal Z\to\mathcal X\times_k\mathcal Z\to\mathcal X\times_k\mathcal X$. Both factors are base changes of $i$, so [lem-sfb-stack-closed-immersion-calculus] makes $j$ a closed immersion and $|j|$ a closed map.

The map $h=\pi\times_k\pi:\mathcal Z\times_k\mathcal Z\to\operatorname{Spec}K\times_k\operatorname{Spec}K$ induces a homeomorphism. Indeed its factorization through $\operatorname{Spec}K\times_k\mathcal Z$ has two factors that are base changes of $\pi$. Each induces a homeomorphism by the universal clause of [lem-sfb-singleton-stack-finite-field-homeomorphism], and their composition is a homeomorphism. Associating products changes no objects: both factorizations send a pair to its two images, with the same compatibility over $k$.

source.place: Tag 06R9 (lemma-gerbe-bijection-points), universal base-change clause; the factorization and composition of homeomorphisms are elementary.

proof.text: Write $\delta:\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}K\times_k\operatorname{Spec}K$ for the scheme diagonal. Its image is a closed singleton: the affine product is $\operatorname{Spec}(K\otimes_kK)$, since a map into it amounts to two $k$-algebra maps from $K$, by [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and the tensor-product universal property. The diagonal corresponds to the surjection $\mu:K\otimes_kK\to K$, $a\otimes b\mapsto ab$, which is onto because $\mu(a\otimes1)=a$. Its kernel is maximal and $V(\ker\mu)=\{\ker\mu\}$ since the quotient is the field $K$. Hence $|\delta|(\operatorname{Spec}K)$ is closed.

source.place: Affine fibre-product construction (lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes); the tensor universal property, multiplication quotient, and Zariski closed singleton are written out.

proof.text: Let $z$ be the unique point of $|\mathcal Z|$. Naturality of the diagonal gives $h\circ\Delta_{\mathcal Z/k}=\delta\circ\pi$, and $j\circ\Delta_{\mathcal Z/k}=\Delta_{\mathcal X/k}\circ i$: on objects these identities send an object to its identical pair with identity comparison. Thus the homeomorphism $|h|$ takes $|\Delta_{\mathcal Z/k}|(z)$ to the closed singleton of step 4. Its inverse image is a closed singleton in $|\mathcal Z\times_k\mathcal Z|$. The closed map $|j|$ of step 2 sends that singleton to $\{|\Delta_{\mathcal X/k}|(x)\}$, which is therefore closed. This proves the assertion for every closed $x$; if $\mathcal X$ is empty there is no point to check.

source.place: Tag 0H20 (lemma-subspace-induced-topology); naturality of diagonals and preservation of closed sets by the cited closed map.
